newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B share index closes sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B share index closes sharply higher.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index rebounded sharply on Monday after last week's falls with investors snapping up stocks in firms expected to post strong results in 1996, brokers said.
The B share index rallied 7.68 points or 6.11 percent to close at 133.24 on volume of 44.69 million shares worth HK$194.31 million against Friday's HK$191.59 million.
Brokers said the rise was fueled by institutional demand for shares of firms expected to report strong earnings this year.
"Institutions built positions in shares with expected promising 1996 results, which boosted market sentiment," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
The average P/E ratio of Shenzhen-listed B shares is now below 20 times, which discouraged selling, brokers said.

"Selling pressure eased on Monday after declines in the past few sessions, and buying focused on blue-chip counters ahead of the corporate reporting season," a broker with a Chinese major brokerage said.
"The index appears to have found support at the 130-point level over the past few days," he added.

The A share market maintained its downward trend on Monday, with selling in cheap and small shares continuing and market sentiment remaining overshadowed by Beijing's stock crackdown last week, brokers said.
The A index declined 6.71 points, or 2.04 percent, to end at 322.25, with turnover rising to 5.12 billion yuan from 4.27 billion yuan on Friday.
On the B share market, SEG became the biggest gainer with a rise of HK$0.45, or 9.47 percent, to HK$5.20 on trade of 1.89 million shares.
